one_liner: Estimate LLM serving speed from model size and GPU bandwidth using prefill/decode physics.

key_terms.definition: The phase that ingests all prompt tokens at once in a single parallel forward pass, producing the first output token; compute-bound.
The phase that generates one new token per step conditioned on all prior tokens, run sequentially; memory-bandwidth-bound.
Stored keys and values for all past tokens, per layer and head, reused across decode steps so they need not be recomputed; trades memory for compute.
Ratio of FLOPs performed to bytes moved from memory (FLOP/byte); determines whether a kernel is compute-bound or memory-bound.
The arithmetic-intensity value (FLOP/s divided by bytes/s) at which a GPU's compute and memory-bandwidth limits cross, separating compute-bound from memory-bound regimes.
Latency from request arrival to the first streamed output token; dominated by prefill compute and queueing delay.
Average time between successive output tokens during decode; dominated by memory-bandwidth-bound decode speed.
The per-step gap between consecutive tokens; the instantaneous value whose average is TPOT.
Upper bound on single-stream tokens/sec, equal to memory bandwidth divided by (model parameter count times bytes per parameter).
Queueing-theory result that average concurrent requests equal arrival rate times average time in system (L = λW); used to size serving throughput from KV-cache capacity and decode latency.
Serving technique that groups multiple sequences' decode steps together so one weight read is amortized across many tokens, raising throughput nearly for free.
Attention variant using fewer key/value heads than query heads, shrinking KV-cache size since cache cost depends only on KV heads, not query heads.

prerequisites: GPU memory hierarchy and HBM bandwidth
